DatasetTitle: Georgian Intercity Bus Routes — Source-backed collection
Scope: Georgian domestic intercity and regional bus/minibus routes, airport shuttles, and selected cross-border terminal listings. Schedule observations are a dated/undated research snapshot, not a live feed.

SqlServerSingleTableSchema.Name: OperatorName
SqlServerSingleTableSchema.Meaning: Carrier name or explicit unresolved provider label

SqlServerSingleTableSchema.Name: DepartureTime
SqlServerSingleTableSchema.Meaning: Local Georgia time; null when only a frequency window is published

SqlServerSingleTableSchema.Name: ArrivalDayOffset
SqlServerSingleTableSchema.Meaning: 0 same calendar day; 1 next day, calculated from listed clocks

SqlServerSingleTableSchema.Name: DurationMinutes
SqlServerSingleTableSchema.Meaning: Calculated from listed departure/arrival clocks when both exist

SqlServerSingleTableSchema.Name: TicketPriceGEL
SqlServerSingleTableSchema.Meaning: Per ticket in GEL; null when source does not publish an amount

SqlServerSingleTableSchema.Name: OperatingDates
SqlServerSingleTableSchema.Meaning: Date range/sample exactly or cautiously normalized from source

SqlServerSingleTableSchema.Name: ViaStops
SqlServerSingleTableSchema.Meaning: Published intermediate stops, in route order where available

SqlServerSingleTableSchema.Name: SchedulePattern
SqlServerSingleTableSchema.Meaning: Published frequency window; not expanded into invented trips

SqlServerSingleTableSchema.Name: EvidenceStatus
SqlServerSingleTableSchema.Meaning: Source quality, date applicability and verification limits

SqlServerSingleTableSchema.Name: SupportingSourceUrl
SqlServerSingleTableSchema.Meaning: Additional context, such as secondary fare corroboration

Limitations: No C# solution/project, SQL Server connection details, or existing table schema were present in the workspace; the live database was not modified. The SQL export defines a generic flat table for review/import.

The supplied ticket.ge URL redirects to TRE.GE. Current TRE provider profiles expose operator route networks, but dynamic date searches do not expose the full all-date timetable; train/bus results may mix on destination pages.
Citybus, Metro Georgia and Georgian Bus publish dated samples, but not every date and route combination was exhaustively queried. Historical sample schedules remain labeled as such.
The Tbilisi terminal schedule is undated and includes a 07:30 Citybus Batumi listing that conflicts with the operator's 08:00 route page. It is retained with an explicit conflict warning.

Kutaisi Travel publishes detailed regional times/fares, but the timetable page does not state an effective date. Frequency windows are stored as patterns and not expanded into individual invented departures.

Marshrutka.info exposes 249 route links in current HTML while its visible heading says 246, and lists 146 city/town nodes. These are third-party route leads; active operation, operator identity and trip schedules are unverified.
Mestia municipality's one-page schedule has no effective date. ProSvaneti is a secondary guide. Rustavi budget figures are aggregate and cannot be allocated to individual trip rows.
International route listings from Tbilisi Central are not full departure schedules; cross-border operator names are included for discovery, but actual carrier/date availability was not verified.
No CAPTCHA, login, or access restriction was bypassed. Some booking interfaces are dynamic and did not expose results in the readable public page extract.
No synthetic service/test records were created. Missing ticket prices, times, durations, stations, days or dates remain null rather than being estimated unless a source explicitly supplied a range.
